First reasoned review: 6958ab4e6136 / 3800d2ba6ebb / 42119ac24bdf

Evidence was obtained with atomscan, cleave facts (including UTF-16 and decoded
strings), pefile, Capstone, and Ghidra native decompilation. No specimen was
executed. The submitted sandbox URLs were inaccessible through the web tool;
the queue's labels and model scores did not decide these verdicts.

6958ab4e613697056fb73e58da3f1e576baff204f46189d66b651f5e850d4a3b
MALICIOUS: damaged Kawaii-Unicorn native VB6 replicator.
At VA 0x42a0d0, native code obtains App.Path and App.EXEName (vtable offsets
0x50 and 0x58), reads the executable through file 1 into a byte SAFEARRAY,
selects an index with Rnd and UBound, and stores index modulo 255 at that
index. The indexed byte store is at VA 0x42a553. The same array is written
through file 2 at 0x42a605; the output path is launched through the runtime
Shell primitive. The other handler at 0x42a770 constructs a random
Unicorn-<number>.exe path and increments a displayed counter.
The routine at 0x42ac40 builds cmd /c rename using App.Path and App.EXEName,
retiring its own image to an App.EXEName + .die destination. This is NOT
proof of arbitrary victim-file destruction. Its destruction finding is
retired. The replacement objective requires native array-write code,
self-path capability, random generation, file read/write, shell execution,
and rename syntax. It requires neither the family name nor the .die suffix.
Family identity remains corroboration in any:, with the behavioral objective
required independently. Two hostile findings remain: behavior and family.
This is a corrupted generation: the .data raw offset exceeds the file, code
and headers contain mutations, and parts of control flow are damaged. The
verdict describes the malicious replication implementation, not a claim that
this exact generation executes every path successfully.
Independent family corroboration (different specimen, not exact-hash proof):
https://www.joesandbox.com/analysis/1720306/1/pdfexecutive
records numerous executable replicas being created and started.

3800d2ba6ebbff2381a999bb1bdc2ea2351dff6c69da0420391a09797bbc6280
BENIGN: DISM host with concatenated ordinary Windows utilities.
The initial PE is DismHost.exe, with native CRT entry 0x10000f3cc leading to
COM security initialization, DISM class registration, an event loop and DISM
core/proxy loading. The DismCorePS.dll loader resolves DllGetDismInterfaces;
there is no path that reads and activates the appended executables.
PE images start at these file offsets:
  0x000000 DismHost.exe
  0x0179ff Oracle Java 7 policytool.exe
  0x01b7a6 UPX 3.91 packer (itself packed)
  0x065fa5 Office Click-to-Run perfboost utility
  0x0b5c6c Adobe LogTransport2.exe
  0x107503 Firefox plugin-hang-ui.exe
  0x1315aa Microsoft App-V mavinject32.exe
  0x18b2d1 7-Zip 19 uninstaller
  0x18eed0 Adobe CRLogTransport.exe
The perfboost image's CRT entry 0x4062f5 reaches 0x40482f, which builds named
synchronization objects, waits, and reports events. Its PDB is
P:\Target\x86\ship\click2run\x-none\perfboost.pdb. A .c2r section is a section
name, not proof of sideloading. UPX includes ELF loader-stub names as packer
data; Adobe telemetry keys, configuration names and User-Agent strings are
ordinary references. None establishes a dropper or concealment objective.
No hostile or suspicious traits fire in the outer file or carved units.
This verdict does not grant an identity-based exception to DISM or its tools.

42119ac24bdf9dc982d51960396fb2785094f14937b36531c544fb053a86d27a
MALICIOUS: StormAttack service-DLL persistence/injection loader.
Entry initialization reaches 0x401cb0. The extraction chain at 0x402460
locates resource 101, copies its data and writes StormServer.dll. The
0x401260 routine replaces LanmanServer\Parameters\ServiceDLL with the
attacker DLL path, rather than merely mentioning the registry location.
0x401150 creates a hidden IE/notepad/calc process, allocates remote memory,
writes the DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA and supplies it plus that path to
CreateRemoteThread. At 0x401900 it registers an Active Setup StubPath,
reads/patches its image and writes a GUID-named copy. 0x401390 gets its module
path, converts it to a short path, constructs COMSPEC /c del ... > nul,
creates the suspended shell and resumes it for self-delete cleanup.
Resource 101 begins at file offset 0x5060 and is 39,936 bytes. It is severely
zeroed: its entry RVA 0x741a and import descriptors contain zeros, despite
surviving Storm DNS/HTTP strings. No DDoS capability or live C2 behavior is
inferred from those strings. The outer loader's concrete unwanted persistence
and injection code justifies MALICIOUS even with this damaged payload.
Four hostile and one suspicious outer findings remain.

Trait placement / regression notes:
- Nine ordinary references/declarations move out of objectives into registry
  key, config path, User-Agent, PDB, section-name and packer-reference homes.
  Matchers, size gates, file/platform scopes and severities are preserved;
  names/descriptions now state only their supported observations.
- Explicit consumers follow the moves. Two broad objective ancestor consumers
  were reviewed: the Python-only staged-loader consumer cannot select these
  PE-only facts; the hosts-sinkhole consumer intentionally loses ordinary
  references as dropper evidence. Neither adds neutral references back as
  attacker evidence.
- To keep existing leaf budgets, the misplaced UPX0 entry-location predicate
  moves from section/label to section/header, retaining its exact scope and
  confidence. Two equivalent includes/indexOf substring-branch matchers merge;
  their sole OR consumer retains the exact union with no count threshold.
- The high e_lfanew matcher formerly skipped another DOS-header-sized span
  after offset 0x3c and inspected DOS-stub bytes. It now tests the high word of
  the actual four-byte field. Ordinary headers no longer fire.
- UTF-16 rename syntax now requires zero high bytes: corrupted high bytes
  encode different characters. The .die co-occurrence is bounded to 128 bytes
  and its description does not assert data flow or victim damage.
- check.py constructs 15 independent benign controls, covering relocated
  references, high/ordinary header offsets, byte/word/data-section stores,
  App method-pair near misses, near/distant rename fragments, corrupted wide
  commands, UPX entry location and both User-Agent substring spellings.
  Every control must have zero hostile findings.
